key_insight: BISECT addresses spectral starvation in continual LoRA learning by splitting a fixed low-rank budget between shared feature directions and task-specific novelty instead of enforcing strict historical-subspace isolation.
engineering_relevance: It supports exemplar-free continual adaptation of pretrained Vision Transformers while merging updates into the backbone with no extra inference parameters or FLOPs.
method: Build an invariant carrier from dominant modes of the joint historical-and-current Gram matrix.
Extract an orthogonal novelty complement using generalized Rayleigh whitening and complement projection.
Merge trained updates using current-to-joint Rayleigh ratios to gate invariant atoms, while retaining novelty atoms at unit gain.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that historical null tails capture only 5.5% of incoming-task variance and that BISECT outperforms prompt, adapter, and LoRA baselines across eight incremental settings on five image datasets.
watch_item: Training-time costs and numerical stability of Gram-matrix decomposition and whitening need assessment; zero added inference cost does not establish low adaptation overhead.
paper_title: BISECT: Bilevel Spectral Decomposition for Low-Rank Continual Learning
